title: 2023 HMMT November Team Problem 5
statement: A complex quartic polynomial \(Q\) is quirky if it has four distinct roots, one of which is the sum of the other three. There are four complex values of \(k\) for which the polynomial \(Q(x)=x^{4}-k x^{3}-x^{2}-x-45\) is quirky. Compute the product of these four values of \(k\).

solutions.text:
Let the roots be \(a, b, c, d\) with \(a+b+c=d\). Since \(a+b+c=k-d\) by Vieta's formulas, we have \(d=k / 2\). Hence

\[0=P\left(\frac{k}{2}\right)=\left(\frac{k}{2}\right)^{4}-k\left(\frac{k}{2}\right)^{3}-\left(\frac{k}{2}\right)^{2}-\left(\frac{k}{2}\right)-45=-\frac{k^{4}}{16}-\frac{k^{2}}{4}-\frac{k}{2}-45 .\]

We are told that there are four distinct possible values of \(k\), which are exactly the four solutions to the above equation; by Vieta's formulas, their product \(45 \cdot 16=720\).
